properties.name: Criterion 1 re-measured after increment 434: 180 of 180 in the top 5 with no exemption left for scan_nodes, held-out paraphrases 34 of 42 (from 36) — three former passes at ranks 6–8, one former miss risen to rank 8, no new miss
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-12 on the real server over stdio, both corpora, after increment 434 rewrote 24 thin descriptions from purpose and described 76 required parameters.

    find_tools top-5, committed corpus (180)
      after 434's first rewrite                       172   ← 8 tools fell out
      after restoring the user-phrased sentence       180   (scan_nodes rose INTO the top 5; its rank-6 exemption removed)
    held-out paraphrases (42, never consulted while writing)
      before 434 (fact of 2026-09-11)                  36 pass /  0 near / 6 miss
      after 434                                        34 pass /  3 near / 5 miss

WHAT THE FIRST REWRITE BROKE, AND WHY IT IS THE RULING WORKING: six of the eight that fell — delete_node, deploy_to, graph_report_markdown, propagate_from, propose_allocation, provides — had lost the one sentence stating the job in a user's words ("remove an item from the design", "this release runs in that environment", "offers that interface"); rewriting "from purpose" had paraphrased it away. The other two — manual_work_report, set_verification_kind — were untouched and slid to rank 6 as their neighbours' descriptions grew. Putting the sentence back on each recovered all eight. That is the discipline dec:a-tool-carries-the-users-phrasing-and-the-corpus-is-the-test names, applied a second time, and the committed corpus catching its absence is what the corpus is for.

THE HELD-OUT MOVEMENT, named: the five misses are the previous six minus design_identity, which rose from miss to rank 8. hierarchy_issues (rewritten in 434, 191 → ~900 chars) and certify_preservation (untouched) slid from the top 5 to ranks 8 and 6. No query newly misses. The net is two former passes now near, one former miss now near — the same class the 2026-09-11 measurement records as the ceiling of word-matching on this surface, where shorter descriptions win on incidental words.

DELIBERATELY NOT TUNED. The held-out set exists to be reported, not chased: adjusting hierarchy_issues to recover a paraphrase would make the held-out set the next thing people tune to, which is the one failure the check was built to prevent. The number is stated instead. graph_report_markdown WAS shortened (826 → 490 chars) — but on the committed corpus, where its substance is documented on graph_report and the long form duplicated it; that is a description being made right, not a score being chased.

BOUNDS: same as the prior fact — both corpora by one author on one day, one phrasing per tool per corpus, the acceptance bar the default top 5. The scorer now also names the near rows (docs/local/tool-sweep/findability/score.py, local), which the prior run could not.
